messages.body:
Hi Solen and Zhen,
Regarding modelling of Mg-DNA-protein systems (for which I wrote about a
month ago) with the fine-tuned 12-6-4 divalent metal ion parameters, I
managed to run the system, but I had to add/change the following
parameters in lj_1264_pol.dat, because the protein has also phosphorylated
amino acids (I used the same polarizability values as for the atoms from
the same atom type in the same hybridization state):
CG 1.352 (the same value as C)
OV 0.637 (the same value as OH and OS)
OT 0.637 (the same value as OH and OS)
Also, because my ligand has aliphatic 3-ring I had to change the
polarizability of atom type "cx" to 1.061 (the value in the original
lj_1264_pol.dat file is 1.352) to be the same as for "c3", because I was
getting an error message: "Polarizability parameter of AMBER_ATOM_TYPE c3
is not the same as that of AMBER_ATOM_TYPE cx, but their VDW parameters
are the same."
Please let me know whether these changes are correct and the results will
be valid.
In addition, as I use Na+ and Cl- ions to neutralize the system and to
obtain 0.152 M solution, please let me know whether I should also add
Li/Merz ion parameters for -1 and +1 ions to the leap file:
frcmod.ions1lm_126_tip4pew or frcmod.ions1lm_1264_tip4pew?
My leap file includes:
source leaprc.protein.ff19SB
source leaprc.DNA.OL15
source leaprc.water.tip4pew
source leaprc.gaff2
source leaprc.phosaa19SB
loadAmberParams frcmod.DNA.OL15
loadAmberParams gaff2.dat
loadAmberParams frcmod.ions234lm_1264_tip4pew
loadamberparams frcmod.tip4pew
And my parmed file is:
setOverwrite True
change AMBER_ATOM_TYPE :A*,DA*.N7 NAMG
change AMBER_ATOM_TYPE :G*,DG*.N7 NGMG
change AMBER_ATOM_TYPE :*.OP* OPMG
addLJType .%NAMG
addLJType .%NGMG
addLJType .%OPMG
add12_6_4 :MG watermodel TIP4PEW polfile
/home/share/iglika/Anthraquinones/MD_Amber/lj_1264_pol_my.dat
printLJMatrix :MG
Thank you in advance
Best regards
Iglika

>

> fine-tuned Panteva parameters for Mg2+ with TIP4P-Ew water.
> But if you are, you should not be getting such error.

> FF in leap:
> source leaprc.protein.ff19SB
> source leaprc.DNA.OL15
> source leaprc.water.tip4pew
> loadamberparams frcmod.ions234lm_1264_tip4pew
>
> followed by parmed lines:
> setOverwrite True
> change AMBER_ATOM_TYPE :A*,DA*.N7 NAMG
> change AMBER_ATOM_TYPE :G*,DG*.N7 NGMG

>
> Either way I hope your issue is resolved and your system builds with
> consistent parameters.

>> Hi Iglika,
>>
>> Everything mentioned, TIP4-EW water and 12-6-4 parameters for divalent
>> metal ions etc., are compatible with proteins.
>> The the fine-tuned parameters (i.e. Panteva corrections) mentioned
>> earlier
>> only make pair-wise adjustments between Mg2+ and the nucleic acid atoms
>> and therefore no other component of the system is affected.
>>
>> You would simply source your protein force field along with the DNA,
>> water
>> and divalent metal ions force fields/parameters and your system should
>> build fine (assuming no unrelated issues). I would still recommend
>> equilibrating your solvent following the nucleic acid tutorials. Once a
>> nucleic acid molecule loses structural properties it almost never can
>> recover it, and these depend highly on the solvent environment around
>> it.
>>
>> Good luck!
>> Solen

>>> we recommend using TIP4P-Ew water model and the fine-tuned 12-6-4

messages.body:
Hi Iglika,
Thank you for emailing the community for a double check. The files look generally correct.
Regarding “whether to add 12-6-4 for Na+ and Cl-”, my short answer is “no”, and “frcmod.ions1lm_126_tip4pew” should be used.
However, if the Na+ and Cl- are doing more than “neutralizing the charge and contributing to the salinity”, like if they are really close to the DNA-protein system (let’s say closer than 2Å), adding 12-6-4 on Na+ and Cl- might be needed. We can worry about that when it happens.
Hope it brings some comfort. Wish all the best.
Regards,
Zhen.

Hi Solen and Zhen,
Regarding modelling of Mg-DNA-protein systems (for which I wrote about a
month ago) with the fine-tuned 12-6-4 divalent metal ion parameters, I
managed to run the system, but I had to add/change the following
parameters in lj_1264_pol.dat, because the protein has also phosphorylated
amino acids (I used the same polarizability values as for the atoms from
the same atom type in the same hybridization state):
CG 1.352 (the same value as C)
OV 0.637 (the same value as OH and OS)
OT 0.637 (the same value as OH and OS)
Also, because my ligand has aliphatic 3-ring I had to change the
polarizability of atom type "cx" to 1.061 (the value in the original
lj_1264_pol.dat file is 1.352) to be the same as for "c3", because I was
getting an error message: "Polarizability parameter of AMBER_ATOM_TYPE c3
is not the same as that of AMBER_ATOM_TYPE cx, but their VDW parameters
are the same."
Please let me know whether these changes are correct and the results will
be valid.
In addition, as I use Na+ and Cl- ions to neutralize the system and to
obtain 0.152 M solution, please let me know whether I should also add
Li/Merz ion parameters for -1 and +1 ions to the leap file:
frcmod.ions1lm_126_tip4pew or frcmod.ions1lm_1264_tip4pew?
My leap file includes:
source leaprc.protein.ff19SB
source leaprc.DNA.OL15
source leaprc.water.tip4pew
source leaprc.gaff2
source leaprc.phosaa19SB
loadAmberParams frcmod.DNA.OL15
loadAmberParams gaff2.dat
loadAmberParams frcmod.ions234lm_1264_tip4pew
loadamberparams frcmod.tip4pew
And my parmed file is:
setOverwrite True
change AMBER_ATOM_TYPE :A*,DA*.N7 NAMG
change AMBER_ATOM_TYPE :G*,DG*.N7 NGMG
change AMBER_ATOM_TYPE :*.OP* OPMG
addLJType @%NAMG
addLJType .%NGMG
addLJType .%OPMG
add12_6_4 :MG watermodel TIP4PEW polfile
/home/share/iglika/Anthraquinones/MD_Amber/lj_1264_pol_my.dat
printLJMatrix :MG
Thank you in advance
Best regards
Iglika

>> Hi Iglika,
>>
>> Everything mentioned, TIP4-EW water and 12-6-4 parameters for divalent
>> metal ions etc., are compatible with proteins.
>> The the fine-tuned parameters (i.e. Panteva corrections) mentioned
>> earlier
>> only make pair-wise adjustments between Mg2+ and the nucleic acid atoms
>> and therefore no other component of the system is affected.
>>
>> You would simply source your protein force field along with the DNA,
>> water
>> and divalent metal ions force fields/parameters and your system should
>> build fine (assuming no unrelated issues). I would still recommend
>> equilibrating your solvent following the nucleic acid tutorials. Once a
>> nucleic acid molecule loses structural properties it almost never can
>> recover it, and these depend highly on the solvent environment around
>> it.
>>
>> Good luck!
>> Solen
